name: Cinnamon-bellied Ground-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Breeds southern chile and southern argentina; winters northward in andes to southern peru
description: Attractive but generally uncommon and rather local terrestrial flycatcher, breeding in Patagonia and migrating north for the winter. Breeds in open grassland, coastal dunes, and gravel steppes, usually with bluffs or rocky outcrops nearby for nesting; winters in open Andean habitats and bogs.

name: Sora
rangeDescription: Southern alaska to northern baja california and southern usa; winters to west indies and northern south america
description: Fairly small rail; short yellow bill, black face, and gray neck distinctive. Found in marshes with grasses or reeds; generally shy but often seen foraging at the edge of shallow water.

name: Black Turnstone
rangeDescription: Breeds coastal alaska; winters southeastern alaska to northwestern mexico
description: Fairly small, stocky shorebird with short, chisel-like bill. Dark charcoal-colored overall with white belly.

name: Blue-crowned Chlorophonia
rangeDescription: Montane forest of southeastern mexico (veracruz) to nicaragua
description: Small, chunky, emerald-green finch of humid evergreen forest in highlands and foothills. Usually in pairs or small groups feeding at fruiting trees and bushes, often in the canopy where easily overlooked.

name: Western Sandpiper
rangeDescription: Breeds siberia and alaska; winters to northern south america
description: Small sandpiper with relatively long, droopy bill (longer on females). In breeding plumage, shows rich rufous tones on shoulders, cheeks, and crown.

name: Brown-rumped Minivet
rangeDescription: Breeds central and southeastern china; winters to thailand and indochina
description: Small gray-brown minivet. Male has bright white face with a dark gray nape and a slender line through the eye.

name: Madagascar Owl
rangeDescription: Forest of madagascar
description: Fairly large, brown owl with long ear tufts. Endemic to Madagascar, where it is found locally in all forest types, and sometimes in scrub and plantations.

name: Gray-headed Sunbird
rangeDescription: Western democratic republic of the congo eastward through uganda and far northwestern tanzania
description: An odd warbler-like sunbird with a long, only slightly downcurved bill. Mostly olive-green with a gray head and a pale throat.

name: Red-throated Caracara
rangeDescription: Far southern mexico to northern bolivia and southern brazil
description: Large, raucous forest raptor. Unmistakable by virtue of its size, social habits, and loud, incessant calls.

name: Princess Parrot
rangeDescription: Dry eucalyptus forest of interior central and western australia
description: Very long-tailed, pastel-toned parrot of arid inland western deserts of Australia, typically only seen by those deliberately searching for it in the remote Great Sandy Desert, although occasionally found closer to Alice Springs or Uluru. Male has glorious blue and lilac crown, pink throat, baby-blue lower belly, lime-green wing coverts, and bright red bill; female similar but colors less intense and extensive.

name: Rufous-throated Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Northern australia (fitzroy river, western australia to noosa, queensland)
description: Small honeyeater with a distinctive red-brown throat patch, white underparts, gray head, brown back, and yellow wing patch. Juveniles lack the rusty throat patch but may have traces of reddish coloration.

name: Waigeo Shrikethrush
rangeDescription: Waigeo (raja ampat islands, off western new guinea)
description: Learn about Little Shrikethrush (Waigeo): explore photos, sounds, and observations collected by birders around the world.

name: Yellow-cheeked Lorikeet
rangeDescription: Montane forest of sulawesi
description: Small bright green lorikeet with bright yellow cheeks. Also note olive-yellow crown, yellow-edged “scaling” on the belly, and bright red bill.

name: Black-chinned Weaver
rangeDescription: Southeastern gabon (lekoni) to central angola and adjacent congo republic
description: A black-backed weaver with a yellow rump and different-looking sexes: the female has a black hood and throat, and the male has a yellow-orange forehead, crown, nape, and neck, with black restricted to the face and throat. An uncommon resident in open bushy savanna with isolated patches of forest between 500 and 1500 meters of elevation, often in disjunct populations.

name: Long-crested Eagle
rangeDescription: Savanna of sub-saharan africa
description: Large, chunky, blackish eagle with a towering, floppy crest. In flight, the wing shows much white below and less above.

name: Spot-backed Antwren
rangeDescription: Far eastern colombia, southern venezuela, and northwestern amazonian brazil
description: Small canopy antwren with a long, graduated tail. Males are largely gray with a black crown and a bold white eyebrow; the black spots on the back can be difficult to see.

name: Semipalmated Sandpiper
rangeDescription: Breeds arctic north america; winters to southern south america
description: Small, grayish-brown sandpiper. Typically shows relatively short, blunt-tipped bill, but this varies across the breeding range: western populations are shortest-billed, eastern populations are longest, and females have longer bills than males!

name: Ecuadorian Seedeater
rangeDescription: Mountains of southwestern colombia (nariño) to northern peru (cajamarca)
description: Scarce and very local. A rather plain, easily overlooked, small seed-eating bird.

name: New Caledonian Imperial-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Montane forest of new caledonia and île des pins
description: Enormous, long-tailed, mostly dark slaty-blue pigeon with dark rufous belly and vent. Tail dark chestnut at the base and dark gray towards the tip.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Pirre Chlorospingus
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of eastern panama
description: Fairly small tanager-like sparrow with an extremely tiny range in the foothills of eastern Panama, from around 800–1,200 m. Distinctive in range: olive-brownish overall with brighter yellow-ochre underparts, darker blackish face, and staring pale eye.
